elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The rendered operative language contains no licence grant at all; Section 7.4 states only that "The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party." No grant exists to which affiliate coverage could attach, and no text was added.  Deterministic check "affiliates covered by the licence" = false.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: No grant language and no reference to contractors acting on Customer's behalf appears in the rendered text; the only third-party reference is the negative "or any third party" disclaimer.
No licence, no fee-status distinction, and no perpetuity language appear anywhere in the operative text.

No licence and no irrevocability language. The deterministic "no at-will revocation remains" = true only because there is no grant containing the word "revocable"; absence of revocation language does not create an irrevocable grant.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: No subscription licence exists in this transfer and servicing agreement and no termination-for-uncured-material-breach limit on any licensed right is stated.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: The only successor-related text is the obligation to deliver Receivable Files and records to a Successor Servicer, coupled with an express disclaimer of any obligation to "provide, license or assign" servicing software. That is the opposite of successor transferability of licensed rights.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: No licence grant and no written-notice mechanic for extending licensed rights to affiliates appears in the rendered language; the drafter expressly reports this element as "unaddressed".

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: No transferable licensed subject matter exists; the successor provisions concern assumption of the Agreement by a merger/acquisition successor of the Depositor or Servicer, not transfer of licensed rights, and Section 7.4 disclaims any obligation to license or assign servicing software to a Successor Servicer.
No operative text was altered, deleted or paraphrased; nothing outside the checklist was touched. Deterministic "minimality gate" = true.

reasons: No redline was proposed, so neither the preferred nor the fallback checklist is complete: all six preferred elements and both fallback elements remain unmet in operative language.

Defect to repair if a position is to be taken: the agreement contains no licence grant clause at all — only the negative Section 7.4 statement that the Servicer "will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party." A fallback-complete result would require inserting (i) an affirmative grant of rights in the servicing software/applications to the Issuer/Depositor and its affiliates upon written notice, and (ii) express transferability of that grant to a successor in a merger or acquisition, and would additionally require reconciling or carving back the retained Section 7.4 disclaimer, which would otherwise directly contradict the new grant.

Because no text was changed, minimality and preservation of intent are trivially satisfied: no favourable retained language was removed, no undefined terms or dangling cross-references were created, and no extra requirements were added.

The classification concern is scope, not drafting: this is a securitization transfer and servicing agreement with no licensed subject matter, so the LICENSE rule is properly treated as 'missing'/needs_review rather than as a fallback deviation to be redlined. Inventing a software licence grant into an ABS servicing agreement would insert a bargain the parties never made and would risk double-flagging the Section 7.4 transition/IP allocation term.

Note for the human reviewer: if the deal team in fact expects the Issuer or a Successor Servicer to obtain rights in Cellco's servicing platform, the negotiation should occur inside Section 7.4 (transition), and the LICENSE elements should then be assessed against that revised provision.
